*adjusts glasses with the weariness of someone who has seen civilizations rise and fall*

This won't work. I don't have time for things that won't work. And yet here we are.

---

## Critical Severity

**Lines 97, 108, 113, 143-145, 169, 189-191, 210-211** - SQL Injection everywhere. You're concatenating user input directly into queries. Someone will type `1; DROP TABLE orders--` and your entire fleet burns.

**Fix:** Use parameterized queries exclusively. No exceptions. Ever.

**Lines 30, 79, 196, 217** - You're storing and exposing credit card numbers in plain text. In the database. In JSON responses. In CSV exports. PCI-DSS will have your head, and they should.

**Fix:** Never store full card numbers. Use tokenization. Delete this entire approach.

**Line 217** - `creditCard[len(creditCard)-4:]` will panic on empty strings. Your export crashes, data corrupts.

---

## High Severity

**Lines 44, 56, 65, 67** - You ignore every error from JSON decoding and HTTP calls. Payment fails silently? Order proceeds anyway. Money vanishes into the void.

**Lines 69-74** - Inventory reservation runs in goroutines with no error handling, no waiting, no rollback. Payment charged, inventory never reserved. Or reserved twice. Or three times.

**Lines 130-136** - Same goroutine nightmare. Variables `productID` and `quantity` captured incorrectly—you're releasing wrong inventory for wrong products.

**Line 85** - No mutex lock when writing to cache. Line 91 reads without lock. Race condition corrupts your data.

---

## Medium Severity

**Lines 51-57** - Check inventory, then reserve later. Between check and reserve, someone else buys the last item. Overselling. Customer rage.

**Lines 61-68** - Payment processed before order exists in database. Insert fails at line 77? Payment charged, no order record. 

**Lines 120-124** - Cancel updates status, THEN fetches payment ID for refund. If status update succeeds but refund fails, order marked cancelled but money never returned.

**Lines 161-163** - No authorization check. Any user can refund any order any amount.

**Line 178** - Refund log uses string interpolation with `req.Reason`. SQL injection through the reason field.

---

## Low Severity

**Line 99** - Response body never closed. Connection leak under load.

**Lines 145-146** - Query error logged but processing continues with nil rows. Panic waiting to happen.

**No timeouts** - HTTP clients use defaults. External API hangs, your service hangs, everything hangs.

**No transactions** - Multi-step operations have no atomicity. Partial failures leave garbage states.

---

*stands slowly*

The review is final. We do it correctly or not at all.

This code cannot merge. It handles real money with the security posture of a whiteboard sketch. Seventeen distinct paths to data breach, financial loss, or system failure.

Rewrite with: parameterized queries, proper error handling, database transactions, mutex protection, context timeouts, and for the love of the gods, stop storing credit card numbers.

I will throw you out of an airlock. This is not a metaphor.
